title: Revolutionizing 6G Wireless Networks with RISs: Enhancements in Sensing and Communications
detail_page_title: [2610.27695v1] Revolutionizing 6G Wireless Networks with RISs: Enhancements in Sensing and Communications
summary: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) have emerged as one of the most promising technologies for the next-generation wireless networks, offering advantages such as cost efficiency, low power consumption, flexible deployment, and large effective aperture. Extensive studies have demonstrated the capabilities of RISs to enhance communication performance, including coverage extension, sum-rate improvement, interference suppression, security enhancement, etc. As 6G networks continue to evolve, wireless sensing is expected to play a pivotal role alongside communication. Undoubtedly, RISs possess great potential to enable seamless integration of sensing and communication by supporting both passive and active sensing paradigms. This paper explores how RISs can revolutionize wireless networks by enhancing both communication and sensing capabilities. Specifically, we highlight the fundamental principles, potential applications, and future trends of RIS-assisted integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), anticipating that RIS-enabled ISAC will become a key enabler in the upcoming 6G era.

title: Attosecond Quantum Optical Spectroscopy of Topological Materials
detail_page_title: [2610.28046v1] Attosecond Quantum Optical Spectroscopy of Topological Materials
summary: High-harmonic generation (HHG) provides an ultrafast probe of quantum materials, yet conventional spectral observables do not generally furnish a common signature of band topology. Here we show that quantum-light-driven HHG opens an additional information channel through the photon statistics of the emitted harmonics. Using the Haldane Chern insulator and the time-reversal-invariant Kane-Mele topological insulator, we calculate helicity-resolved equal-time intensity correlations and identify a common enhancement of high-order harmonic correlations in the topological phases. For the Haldane model, a dichroic correlation constructed from opposite helicity channels reverses sign with the Chern number. These signatures originate from the distinct nonlinear response sampled by quantum fluctuations of the driving field and are absent from the corresponding mean harmonic spectra as a common classifier. Our results establish photon-correlation spectroscopy as a route to interrogate topological matter with quantum light and provide a bridge between strong-field solid-state physics and quantum optics.

title: Phase-Coherent Multistatic Sensing under Phase Noise in Distributed ISAC
detail_page_title: [2610.28816v1] Phase-Coherent Multistatic Sensing under Phase Noise in Distributed ISAC
summary: We investigate phase-coherent multistatic sensing in distributed ISAC systems where spatially separated access points (APs) share a common, non-ideal local oscillator (LO) impaired by phase noise (PN). In the presence of a single transmit AP and multiple receive APs with OFDM transmission, we derive the joint statistics of PN across receive APs and reveal its unique covariance structure that depends on target location through propagation delays of individual bistatic links. Based on this statistical characterization, we carry out a Cramér-Rao bound analysis of three receiver models, namely PN-free, PN-aware and PN-ignorant, for both isotropic and non-isotropic targets. Simulation results verify the location-dependent statistics of PN in shared-LO distributed architectures while demonstrating how transmit power, LO quality, AP deployment and scattering characteristics affect multistatic localization.

title: Quasi-Phase-Matched Second Harmonic Generation in Poling-Free Lithium Niobate Microrings with Surface Molecular Pattern
detail_page_title: [2610.29417v1] Quasi-Phase-Matched Second Harmonic Generation in Poling-Free Lithium Niobate Microrings with Surface Molecular Pattern
summary: Thin film lithium niobate (TFLN) is a promising integrated photonic platform owing to its large quadratic nonlinearity enabling vital applications such as second-harmonic generation (SHG), optical parametric amplification, and spontaneous parametric down-conversion. However, to achieve high SH conversion efficiency, quasi-phase matching (QPM) through periodic electrical poling is typically required, which remains challenging in certain applications like multiple-ring coupled devices. Here, we demonstrate a surface molecule patterning strategy to enable QPM in a poling-free TFLN microring for SHG. An on-chip normalized conversion efficiency of approximately 11.5%/W is obtained in the poling-free TFLN microring with surface molecular pattern, showing an approximate 400-fold improvement compared to the same microring without surface molecular pattern. This approach offers a versatile route to engineer interfacial nonlinear interactions for nonlinear optics and quantum photonics applications and may be extended to multiple-ring coupled resonators and other platforms.

title: Passive Phase-Aware Hadamard Decoding: Analytical and Machine-Learning Approaches
detail_page_title: [2610.29797v1] Passive Phase-Aware Hadamard Decoding: Analytical and Machine-Learning Approaches
summary: Hadamard-coded optical receivers typically rely on stable interference conditions, which can motivate active optical phase control. We investigate a fixed, intensity-only decoder that embeds four populated modes in an eight-mode interferometer and provides six complementary trigonometric observables through simultaneous power measurements. An analytic transition decoder uses the resulting sign-change patterns without continuous optical phase stabilization. The receiver's intensity-to-observable map is inverted exactly, and an identifiability analysis characterizes exceptional phase configurations and conditional noise sensitivity. An ideal, equal-photon-budget comparison with conventional four-port Hadamard decoding illustrates the potential value of the additional outputs without implying an unconditional advantage. Measurements on programmable photonic processors give 96.19% accuracy for the analytical decoding experiment; a complementary machine-learning analysis reports 98.31% on a held-out experimental trace. These results demonstrate an intensity-only, phase-aware approach to differential Hadamard decoding under the tested conditions, while larger codebooks and hardware-level energy benefits remain topics for future investigation.

title: Structured PARAFAC Channel Estimation for Flexible Intelligent Metasurface Receivers
detail_page_title: [2610.27445v1] Structured PARAFAC Channel Estimation for Flexible Intelligent Metasurface Receivers
summary: Flexible intelligent metasurfaces (FIMs) create geometric diversity through aperture morphing, but their configuration-dependent responses complicate uplink channel estimation. This letter considers multiple users sharing a common angular response and develops a structured PARAFAC model across calibrated FIM configurations. Its known identity factor and rank-one pilot-weighted channel factor enable deterministic, noniterative algebraic factor recovery through per-element rank-one approximations, reference-state normalization, global rank-one projection, and a least-squares morphing-factor update. The recovered spatial and morphing factors are then jointly matched to the calibrated manifold to estimate the common angles, user gains, and configuration-dependent channels. Simulations demonstrate accurate recovery and show that out-of-plane morphing resolves the azimuth-sign ambiguity of an undeformed planar aperture; an angular-spread experiment quantifies the mismatch when the common-response assumption is relaxed.
